style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" Alert BEFORE data is at risk." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="70" width="990" x="900" y="1040" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-56" edge="1" parent="1" source="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-27" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;html=1;endArrow=block;endFill=1;strokeWidth=2;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=11;fontColor=#d79b00;labelBackgroundColor=#ffffff;dashed=1;fontSize=15;fontStyle=1;exitX=0.53;exitY=1;entryX=0.15;entryY=0;" target="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-51" value="⑨ closed segments age out"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-57" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=16;fontColor=#222222;fontStyle=1;spacing=4;" value="How to read it — follow the numbers" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="900" x="40" y="1170" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-58" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Write path (①–⑥)</b><br>① Producer picks a partition: hash(key) % N, then batches and compresses.<br>② The batch goes to that partition's LEADER (found via metadata).<br>③ Leader appends to the active segment, assigns offsets, drops duplicates (producer_id + seq).<br>④ Followers PULL the new data and append it to their own copies.<br>⑤ When every in-sync replica has it, the HIGH WATERMARK moves forward = committed.<br>⑥ Leader acks the producer (with acks=all).<br><br><b>Why pull-based replication + ISR?</b> The leader never waits on a slow follower: it just drops it from the ISR. Durability = "all CURRENT ISR members have it"." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="370" width="610" x="40" y="1210" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-59" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Read path &amp; control (⑦–⑨, C1–C3)</b><br>⑦ Consumers fetch from the leader (long-poll), only up to the high watermark, via zero-copy.<br>⑧ After processing, they commit their offset to __consumer_offsets.<br>⑨ Retention / compaction / tiering work on old closed segments in the background.<br>C1–C3 Admin changes → controller (Raft) → pushed to brokers; clients ask the controller who leads which partition.<br><br><b>If a leader dies:</b> the controller elects a new leader from the ISR → no committed message is lost. Clients refresh metadata and continue.<br><br><b>Trade-offs to say out loud:</b> acks=all = safer but slower · more partitions = more parallelism but more metadata and slower recovery · order only per partition." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="370" width="610" x="670" y="1210" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-60" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Build it in this order</b><br>1. Single-node log: append-only segments + sparse index (offset → file position)<br>2. Network server: produce &amp; fetch APIs, batching, page cache<br>3. Partitions: hash(key) → many logs, spread across brokers<br>4. Replication: leader/follower, pull fetch, ISR, high watermark, leader epochs<br>5. Consumer groups: coordinator, rebalance, offsets topic<br>6. Controller: metadata in Raft, leader election, broker registry<br>7. Retention, then compaction, then tiered storage<br>8. Idempotent producer, then transactions (exactly-once)<br><br><b>Each stage is usable on its own</b> — and each exists because of one earlier decision: <i>append-only log → partitions → replicas → groups → controller.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="370" width="630" x="1300" y="1210" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div:
Partition P0 — LEADER log
append-only, split into segments:
[seg 0 closed] [seg 1 closed] [seg 2 ACTIVE]
each segment = .log + sparse .index + .timeindex
offset = a message's position in the log
sequential writes; durability comes from replication, not fsync per message

Leader state
ISR = in-sync replicas
LEO per replica
HIGH WATERMARK = last offset all ISR have = what is committed

div.div: How to read it — follow the numbers

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 592px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1387px; margin-left: 114px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Write path (①–⑥)
① Producer picks a partition: hash(key) % N, then batches and compresses.
② The batch goes to that partition's LEADER (found via metadata).
③ Leader appends to the active segment, assigns offsets, drops duplicates (producer_id + seq).
④ Followers PULL the new data and append it to their own copies.
⑤ When every in-sync replica has it, the HIGH WATERMARK moves forward = committed.
⑥ Leader acks the producer (with acks=all).
Why pull-based replication + ISR? The leader never waits on a slow follower: it just drops it from the ISR. Durability = "all CURRENT ISR members have it".

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 592px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1387px; margin-left: 744px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Read path & control (⑦–⑨, C1–C3)
⑦ Consumers fetch from the leader (long-poll), only up to the high watermark, via zero-copy.
⑧ After processing, they commit their offset to __consumer_offsets.
⑨ Retention / compaction / tiering work on old closed segments in the background.
C1–C3 Admin changes → controller (Raft) → pushed to brokers; clients ask the controller who leads which partition.
If a leader dies: the controller elects a new leader from the ISR → no committed message is lost. Clients refresh metadata and continue.
Trade-offs to say out loud: acks=all = safer but slower · more partitions = more parallelism but more metadata and slower recovery · order only per partition.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 612px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1387px; margin-left: 1374px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Build it in this order
1. Single-node log: append-only segments + sparse index (offset → file position)
2. Network server: produce & fetch APIs, batching, page cache
3. Partitions: hash(key) → many logs, spread across brokers
4. Replication: leader/follower, pull fetch, ISR, high watermark, leader epochs
5. Consumer groups: coordinator, rebalance, offsets topic
6. Controller: metadata in Raft, leader election, broker registry
7. Retention, then compaction, then tiered storage
8. Idempotent producer, then transactions (exactly-once)
Each stage is usable on its own — and each exists because of one earlier decision: append-only log → partitions → replicas → groups → controller.
